citations.narrative:
Three Cavalier King Charles Spaniel female dogs, each approximately 6 years old, did not have individual identification.
The dogs were not wearing collars and have not been assigned a tag number at the time of inspection. The facility
representative stated they are not microchipped. The facility obtained these dogs approximately 1-2 months ago.
Identification is important in order to maintain inventory of animals, as well as tracing medical, breeding, and sales
records, or in cases of theft or loss. Correct by ensuring all live dogs held on the premises shall be identified by an official
tag of the type described in 2.51 affixed to the animal’s neck by means of a collar or by a distinctive and legible tattoo or
microchip as accepted by the Administrator. Correct by: July 23, 2026.

APHIS form 7005 was missing the date that four dogs were acquired including 1 Goldendoodle and 3 Cavalier King
Charles Spaniel adult dogs. Inaccurate, missing, and/or incomplete records can hinder various aspects of animal
husbandry including the tracking and tracing of animals. To ensure accurate record keeping the applicant shall maintain
records or forms which fully and correctly disclose the required information for the acquisition of animals.
Correct by: July 23, 2026

The surfaces of the indoor portion of the sheltered housing facilities are not being cleaned and sanitized in an appropriate
manner. There are many cobwebs present on the ceiling and cage bars and a buildup of excessive hair at the edges of
the enclosure and under the enclosure that is housing three adult dogs. There is also accumulation of dark brown organic
debris and dirt at the entry/exit door of this enclosure. Surfaces of housing facilities must be cleaned and sanitized when
necessary to satisfy generally accepted husbandry standards and practices. Improper cleaning and sanitization can
increase the risk of contamination and spread of disease hazards to the dogs. The licensee must ensure that hard
surfaces with which the dogs come in contact are spot-cleaned daily and sanitized in accordance with 3.11(b) to prevent
the accumulation of excreta and reduce disease hazards.
Correct by: July 23, 2026

The outdoor run of a sheltered housing enclosure (housing one adult female goldendoodle with tag “13A” and her three
puppies) has a plastic white divider placed vertically against the wire paneling separating the outdoor portions of
neighboring enclosures. This divider has been broken and there are sharp points and edges present. Sharp points and
edges can put the animals at risk for injuries. The facility must ensure that primary enclosures are constructed and
maintained so that they have no sharp points and edges that could injure the dogs.
Correct by: July 23, 2026

A complete head to tail physical examination was not performed for each dog every 12 months as required by the Animal
Welfare Act. Three adult dogs (Sally, Frosty, and Christi) have not had a physical examination since 2022, according to
records obtained verbally by the Attending Veterinarian’s Office. Routine physical examinations are important in that a
veterinarian can inform the licensee of health issues the dogs may be experiencing, can lead to more timely diagnosis
and treatment of issues, and allows APHIS inspectors to ensure adequate veterinary care is being provided to the dogs.
Correct by ensuring all dogs have a complete physical examination by the veterinarian at least every 12 months. Correct
by: August 10, 2026.

The facility is not following their Program of Vet Care for preventative care in dogs.
Three adult dogs (Frosty, Christi and Sally) are overdue for rabies vaccination. A 3-year rabies vaccine was last given in
July 2022 and was due to be given in July 2025. The vaccine is a year overdue.
Male dog, Frosty, last had a distemper/parvovirus vaccine in November 2024. The PVC states this vaccine should be
given “annually”, so it was due in November 2025.
Female dog, Sally, last had the distemper/parvovirus vaccine in February 2025. The PVC states this vaccine should be
given “annually”, so it was due in February 2026.
Female dog, Malty, was last vaccinated for distemper on November 2024. The PVC states this vaccine should be given
“annually”, so it was due in November 2025.
The facility is overdue for fecal and heartworm sampling. The Program of Vet Care states these tests should be
performed on 10% of the adult dogs yearly (according to written and verbal attending veterinarian instructions). These
tests were last performed in January 2025 and were due again in January 2026.
The Animal Welfare Act requires vaccines for contagious and/or deadly diseases, such as rabies, distemper, and
parvovirus, be given to dogs at licensed facilities in accordance with a schedule approve by the attending veterinarian.
Additionally, since some parasites can be passed from dog to dog, the routine fecal and heartworm sampling is a
screening test for parasites and can help with early detection and treatment options.
Correct by ensuring the facility must follow an approved vaccination, fecal, and heartworm testing schedule from the
attending veterinarian. Correct by: July 23, 2026

The facility is not maintaining complete medical records for all of the vaccines required by the Animal Welfare Act and the
Program of Vet Care.
Records for rabies vaccination in 7 adult dogs (3 unnamed female Cavalier King Charles Spaniels, Daisy, Sally, Frosty,
and Christi) were not able to be reviewed at the time of inspection because they had not been obtained by the
veterinarian’s office by the licensee. According to verbal veterinary records, 3 dogs (Sally, Frosty, and Christi) were given
3-year rabies vaccines in July 2022. One dog (Daisy) was given a 3-year rabies vaccine in February 2025.
The three unnamed Cavalier King Charles Spaniels had been obtained by the facility 1-2 months ago and had no vaccine
records to review. Female dog “13A” did not have a medical record that was available for review because it could not be
found.
Complete medical records allow APHIS inspectors to ensure the facility is following their written program of vet care and
the Animal Welfare Act. Correct by ensuring dealers keep copies of medical records for dogs and make the records
available for APHIS inspection. In addition to the identification of the animal, complete medical records must include the
names of all vaccines and treatments administered and the dates of administration. Correct by: June 23, 2026.

The licensee did not maintain records from the annual examination, heartworm, or fecal testing performed in January and
February 2025 for the adult dog Daisy. Not having documentation of all exams and records of all tests that are completed
doesn't allow the APHIS inspector to ensure the licensee is following the Program of Vet Care. The dates and
findings/results of the annual exams and heartworm and fecal testing must be documented and be available to the APHIS
inspector to review during inspection.
Correct by: July 23, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Richard Burdeaux, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
